title: Feelings and body clues
subject: RSHE

thread_tags.line: Thread tags: SMSC S/M/So (C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
thread_tags.rationale: S: reflect on a fictional person’s needs and choices. M: consider caring and helpful actions. So: listen to different possible responses. IL: respect a choice to pause or use a response aid. MR: respect different families and feelings without ranking people.

label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Recognise comfort or discomfort and choose a helpful response.
display_objective: Spot how a young person may feel. Choose a helpful act.
approved_activity: Match fictional situations to feeling words and possible body clues, allowing different responses.
Choose whether the person could pause, ask a question or seek help, and explain the choice.
calendar_note: Year A. 9–13 November 2026. One 40-minute lesson. No day or clock slot inferred. Week 7 is assessing.
where_this_leads: This helps me notice when I need a pause or support during a task.
unit: Caring relationships, feelings and helpful responses
accreditation: The qualification and the accredited unit: staff confirm any mapping from actual work. No criteria or completion are inferred.
assessment: Weeks 1–6 are formative. Week 7 is the assessing lesson. Keep actual responses, support, gaps and next steps in the evidence record.

sources.note: The owner-approved standalone RSHE outline is the weekly teaching source. The three build notes apply throughout. No separate workbook row is asserted.

authoring_provenance.note: Newly authored tasks from the owner-approved RSHE outline. No separate weekly workbook row is asserted. All prompts use fictional cases.

external_sources.note: Approval, curriculum context, template and authored visual provenance.

evidence.description: Two scenario responses and a selected help or pause action, with reasoning and prompts recorded.
evidence.status: not prefilled; actual response and support to be recorded

routes.Supported: Supported: work through two stories with two feeling and action choices at a time; read or scribe as needed.
routes.Independent: Independent: record two story responses, each with a possible feeling, a stated clue and a reason for a helpful response.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: explain a second plausible response or why a clue cannot prove a feeling; add a further help step.

vocab.definition: How a person feels at a time.
A sign that may help explain something.
Not at ease; tight or on edge.
A sense of ease or feeling settled.
Support with a need or task.

cases.text: A young person says a task feels too much. Their hands feel tight.
cases.judgement: Tense or worried could fit. Pause and ask for help.
cases.next_step: Use the stated difficulty and tight hands. Accept a question or a small-step request with a reason.

cases.text: A young person does not know the next step. Their shoulders feel tight.
cases.judgement: Unsure or tense could fit. Ask a question or seek help.
cases.next_step: The key need is the unclear next step. Do not demand the exact emotion word.

cases.text: A young person says they feel at ease. Their hands rest loosely.
cases.judgement: Calm or comfortable could fit. Continue by choice, with help available.
cases.next_step: Comfort is supported by the person’s words. The body clue alone would not prove it.

cases.text: A young person will try a new game. Their heart beats fast.
cases.judgement: Excited, worried or unsure could fit. Ask or pause if wanted.
cases.next_step: There is no single correct feeling. The context and the person’s own words matter.

cases.text: A young person asks to pause. An adult gives time and checks what help is wanted.
cases.judgement: A helpful response that respects choice.
cases.next_step: The pause is not a punishment or something to earn.

cases.text: A young person still needs help. The first adult is busy.
cases.judgement: Ask another trusted adult or use the agreed help route.
cases.next_step: A first unsuccessful request does not mean the person must stop seeking help.

RSHE-BUILD-A2-W02 · Year A · Week beginning 9 November 2026
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Thread tags: SMSC S/M/So (C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
Staff brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Every teaching prompt concerns a fictional young person. Never ask learners about their own bodies, families or experiences, or use a real person as the case. Read fictional cards without inviting comparison with home. No touching, body checking, forced eye contact, acting out distress or personal role-play. Allow a pass, quiet response or pause. If a learner raises a personal concern, follow the setting’s safeguarding procedure; do not turn the disclosure into lesson evidence. Staff use the setting’s agreed support arrangements.

Space: calm seating and clear resources. Voice: an optional response about the fictional case. Audience: an adult listens or reads and responds. Influence: record any change to the task support or next teaching step. A pass is respected and does not require an explanation.
